sketches.title: The Helpful Camp Report
sketches.premise: A tent peg drops at camp, and the campground reporter explains what happens next. Take turns adding one plain event; the trouble should grow while the report stays earnest and gently funny.
sketches.criterion: A move follows if it is the next event caused by the standing camp trouble and adds a new problem to report; a skipped cause, a wrap-up, an undo, or a newcomer the scene could not hold fails.
sketches.move_shape: Write one sentence beginning with "Then," naming one visible event and its cause, such as: "Then the loose peg rolls downhill and knocks over the water jug."
sketches.first_card: The first tent peg slips from a camper's hand and lands in the grass.

sketches.title: The Trail Map That Keeps Changing
sketches.premise: A camping group follows a hand-drawn map after the first tent peg is dropped. Each turn changes one thing about where the group is or what blocks the route, so the map becomes a cheerful record of wrong turns.
sketches.criterion: A move follows if it is one next location or route change caused by the current map situation and preserves every established landmark; jumping past travel, declaring the trip over, reversing a change, or adding a person or place the map cannot support fails.
sketches.move_shape: Write one sentence beginning with "Then," giving the next map change, such as: "Then the path bends around the fallen sign and leads to a muddy bridge."
sketches.first_card: The tent peg drops beside the trail map, and a gust folds the map in half.

sketches.title: The Pack Says Otherwise
sketches.premise: The campers try to set up after dropping the first tent peg, but every useful object is hiding, tangled, borrowed, or in the wrong place. Add one next gear problem or discovery at a time, with a straight-faced camp-guide voice.
sketches.criterion: A move follows if one gear event directly results from the standing gear situation and creates a new task; a missing middle action, a complete fix, an undo, or an object or helper that the packed scene could not contain fails.
sketches.move_shape: Write one sentence beginning with "Then," naming the next gear event, such as: "Then the rope pulled from the bag brings the cooking spoon with it."
sketches.first_card: The first tent peg drops, and it rolls under the open camping pack.

sketches.title: Forecast: Slightly More Camp
sketches.premise: A calm camping trip starts with a dropped tent peg, while an earnest forecast explains how small weather changes affect the camp. Players take turns adding one weather-caused event, keeping the jokes aimed at the campers' choices.
sketches.criterion: A move follows if the next weather event plainly causes a new camp effect while fitting the weather already described; a skipped weather change, a final safe outcome, a reversal, or a new condition the scene has not earned fails.
sketches.move_shape: Write one sentence beginning with "Then," linking weather to one new effect, such as: "Then the light rain fills the peg hole and sends a tiny stream toward the sleeping bags."
sketches.first_card: The first tent peg drops just as a cool breeze crosses the campsite.

sketches.title: Important Camp Notices
sketches.premise: After a tent peg drops, the camp notice board records every official response. Take turns posting the next notice as the small mistake creates larger rules, lines, warnings, and duties, all in a serious but friendly voice.
sketches.criterion: A move follows if it is the next notice caused by the current posted situation and changes what campers must do; a notice that skips its reason, closes the matter, cancels an earlier notice, or introduces a group or rule the board could not know fails.
sketches.move_shape: Write one notice beginning with "Then," stating its reason and effect, such as: "Then, because the peg is missing, the ranger posts a search area around the fire ring."
sketches.first_card: The first tent peg drops, and no one can see where it landed.

sketches.title: The Honest Camp Ledger
sketches.premise: A camping trip keeps a cheerful ledger of what the group has, spends, loses, and must replace after the first tent peg is dropped. Each turn adds one next change to the shared camp supplies, with gentle commentary about every poor choice.
sketches.criterion: A move follows if one recorded supply change is directly caused by the current supplies and leaves a new shortage, need, or choice; an unexplained jump, a full restock or ending, restoring an earlier loss, or adding supplies the camp could not have fails.
sketches.move_shape: Write one sentence beginning with "Then," recording one cause and one new result, such as: "Then the search for the peg uses the last flashlight battery, so the dark box stays unopened."
sketches.first_card: The first tent peg drops, and the campers mark one peg as missing on their supply list.
